requirement: Rendered JavaScript discovery and offline mirroring within Site Grabber, preserving the existing project workflow.
findings: Browser session completion transfers Origin, UserAgent, Cookies and LogoutPages only.
Native session completion validates and protects that session but accepts no rendered-page snapshot.
Grabber fetches response HTML and scans bounded static script references; no rendered DOM provider is integrated.
implementationRequirements: Advertise a native capability and define a bounded rendered-page response contract before enabling browser-side handoff.
Bind every response to project, requested URL, tab/frame and navigation generation; reject stale or cross-project results.
Feed rendered references through existing location/type/size/depth/duplicate filters, parent mapping and checkpoint machinery.
Handle navigation, cancellation, browser closure, timeout and restart explicitly.
Keep rendered discovery and saved offline documents coherent, including dynamically inserted resource URLs.
acceptanceCases: A link assembled by JavaScript at runtime is discovered and downloaded; a static-only control shows the difference.
Navigation during capture rejects the stale page result.
Links outside project scope and logout targets remain excluded.
Stop and resume preserve visited pages and selected files without duplicate jobs.
Downloaded rendered pages navigate offline with their selected resources.
limitations: This is a current-source gap audit and implementation contract, not an implementation or runtime parity claim.
